request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 17:
A: On sync-enabled refreshes, minimumTokenResponseSchema accepts a payload without refresh_token and the parseRefreshTokenResponse default injects refresh_token="refresh_token", which is then spread into o365AuthCredentials and persisted via prisma.credential.update. The Office365 credential row is overwritten with a garbage refresh_token on the first sync-enabled refresh; the next refresh sends that garbage to Microsoft, which rejects it, and the integration is permanently broken with the root cause invisible in logs (the previous console.error for parse failures was also deleted).
B: When the parsed response lacks refresh_token (always true for the sync endpoint, whose documented response contains only access_token and expiry), the function mutates data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, and callers (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts ~98-101, office365calendar CalendarService.ts ~263-270) then persist this merged/stripped object over the credential key via prisma.credential.update. Sync-mode refreshes overwrite the stored credential with a placeholder refresh_token and drop expiry_date and other real fields; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ever removed or the sync endpoint is down, previously-working Google and Outlook credentials are permanently broken (no valid refresh_token to fall back to).

PAIR 18:
A: Success is decided by `response.statusText !== "OK"`; undici's fetch returns an empty statusText when the response carries no reason phrase (e.g. over HTTP/2 or via certain proxies), so a valid 200 response is treated as a failure. Salesforce token refresh intermittently throws HttpError 400 on successful responses depending on protocol/proxy path; `response.ok` (or a status check) is the reliable predicate.
B: The constructor now unconditionally performs a Salesforce token refresh on every service instantiation and gates success on response.statusText !== "OK", which is empty-string for most fetch/undici responses on non-2xx and can be empty even on 2xx depending on runtime. Every Salesforce calendar operation issues a network token refresh before doing any work; when statusText is empty (common under Node 18 fetch), the service throws HttpError 400 and the entire Salesforce integration stops working after this deploy, with no rollback path since the check runs on the hot path.
